environment: Apple M4, Darwin arm64, Go 1.27.3, CGO_ENABLED=0; profiles are local synthetic FP32 fixture exploration, not real-model serving throughput.

fixed64_process_counter_check.interpretation: Native-frame attribution remains strongly skewed even though process counters are mostly user time. One paired observational check does not establish profiler overhead or its cause; do not equate native wait/signal sample percentages with removable wall-clock overhead.

block_profile.interpretation: Delay sums include concurrent goroutines, idle worker receives and testing harness waits; they are not CPU time or additive removable generation latency. Dispatch/completion boundaries remain an investigation target, not a proven bottleneck percentage.

next_hypotheses: Primary: FP32 decode currently accumulates one output dot product at a time. Test sharing each input value across two output accumulators, preserving ascending input-index accumulation order independently for each output. Keep the existing four-sequence-row prefill path, worker count, task partition and thresholds unchanged. Require bit-exact tests for odd output tails, remainder rows and serial/parallel calls before timing.

Secondary: distinguish actual executor dispatch/completion cost from necessary math/idle waits using matched same-process kernel controls and independent profiling methods. Do not repeat earlier caller-participation/threshold ideas without new evidence.
limitations: CPU sampling includes benchmark setup and calibration outside benchmark timers. Profiles change scheduling and are not per-op latency breakdowns. Four-thread and one-thread measurements are different execution configurations, not before/after optimized code. No production change or speedup claim is made in this exploration. Raw binary/profiles stay in ignored runs/; SHA-256 bindings and observations are recorded here.
